periods.name: Ahom period
periods.summary: The Tai-Ahom kingdom of Upper (Ujoni) Assam, founded by Sukaphaa in 1228 and ended by the Burmese invasions and the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826: its kings, queens, nobles and rebels, and the foreign commanders they fought.

characters.name: Chaolung Sukaphaa
characters.summary: Born around 1189 in Mong Mao, he left in 1215, crossed the Patkai hills and reached Namrup in December 1228, founding the Ahom kingdom that lasted until 1826. He built Charaideo in 1253.
characters.notes: Married daughters of the Moran chief Badaucha and the Barahi chief Thakumatha. Moved his base from 1236 (Mungklang) through Habung (1240) and Ligirigaon (1244) before Charaideo.

scenes.title: First View of the Brahmaputra Valley
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa and scouts view the immense, fertile Brahmaputra River plain ('Mung Dun Sun Kham' - Country of Golden Gardens), recognizing its potential for wet-rice cultivation.

scenes.title: Sukaphaa Enters the Assam Valley
scenes.summary: Formal arrival of Sukaphaa's royal entourage in the plains of Upper Assam along the Dihing river basin in 1228 CE, officially inaugurating the 600-year Ahom Dynasty.
scenes.notes: Arrival at Namrup in December 1228. In the same year Sandhya took the throne of Kamarupa.

scenes.title: Establishment of the First Tai Settlements
scenes.summary: Initial settlements established at Tipam, Habung, and Shimolguri; stilt houses (Rwan-hon) constructed and virgin floodplains cleared for agriculture.

scenes.title: The Sacred Promontory of Charaideo
scenes.summary: The sacred royal compound and ancestral temples at Charaideo, the spiritual center and eternal resting place of Ahom royalty.

scenes.title: Institution of the Supreme Offices of Burhagohain and Borgohain
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa institutes the Great Council of Nobles: Thaomung Klinglunmang (Burhagohain) and Thaomung Kangngan (Borgohain), forming a hereditary prime-ministerial council.

scenes.title: Matrimonial Alliances with Borahi and Moran Rulers
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa adopts an assimilative policy by establishing matrimonial bonds with the indigenous Moran chief Bodousa and the Borahi king Thakumtha, marrying local princesses and integrating them into court governance.

scenes.title: Introduction of Advanced Wet-Rice Cultivation (Sali Kheti)
scenes.summary: Introduction of advanced Tai hydraulic techniques, dyke bunding, canal irrigation, and deep-water transplanted Sali rice, producing an agricultural surplus.

scenes.title: Founding and Construction of the Sacred Capital at Charaideo
scenes.summary: In 1253 CE, Sukaphaa establishes the permanent royal capital at Charaideo (Che-Rai-Doi), consecrated with sacred Tai Phuralong rituals and ancestral invocations.

scenes.title: Writing of the First Ahom Buranji (Royal Chronicles)
scenes.summary: Sukaphaa decrees that royal scribes and priests record every event, battle, decree, and genealogy on Sanchi bark (agarwood paper), establishing Assam's Buranji tradition.

scenes.title: The Royal Court of Sukaphaa
scenes.summary: Convening of the sovereign assembly at Charaideo; state administration organized with local leaders integrated, establishing a harmonious multi-ethnic polity.

scenes.title: Institution of Royal Moidams (Pyramidal Earth Tumuli)
scenes.summary: Upon Sukaphaa's demise in 1268 CE, the tradition of building subterranean vaulted brick/stone chambers covered by hemispherical earthen mounds (Moidams) begins at Charaideo.

characters.name: Sudangphaa (Bamuni Konwar)
characters.summary: Son of Tyao Khamti, raised by a Brahmin family in Habung after his mother's execution; found and enthroned at about fifteen in 1397. He introduced the Singarigharutha coronation (1403) and let Hindu rites into the court.
characters.notes: Peace treaty fixing the Patkai boundary in 1401; capital moved to Charguwa in 1403.

scenes.title: Ministers Discover the Hidden Prince Sudang at Habung

scenes.title: Triumphant Royal Return of Sudang to Charaideo

scenes.title: The Reign of Bamuni Konwar
scenes.summary: Sudangphaa rewards his Brahmin foster father and brothers with high court offices, inaugurating Hindu Brahminical influence.

scenes.title: Institution of the Singari-Gharutha Coronation
scenes.summary: Sudangphaa inaugurates the sacred Singari-gharutha ceremony, ascending a raised platform of Singari timber, washing in sacred waters, and killing a bull/buffalo.

scenes.title: The Feast Trap for the Tipam Conspirators

scenes.summary: The rival claimant Tai Sulai returns with a Mong Kawng (Mungkang) army led by the defector Tasim Pou. Sudangphaa meets it near Kuhiarbari in the Tipam country and defeats it, though he is lightly wounded by a spear.

scenes.title: Nangchukham Borgohain Marches on Kamata
scenes.summary: Tai Sulai flees to Kamata. Sudangphaa's commander Nangchukham Borgohain invades, and the Kamata king, also pressed by Bengal, makes peace and gives a daughter in marriage to Sudangphaa.
scenes.notes: Chronology of the Kamata episode is undated and disputed. Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive.

scenes.title: Administrative Centralization at Charagua
scenes.summary: Constructs the new capital city Charagua on the Dihing river to better oversee burgeoning agricultural lands and trade routes.

scenes.title: Cultural Renaissance and Literary Patronage
scenes.summary: Sudangphaa patronizes both Tai chroniclers and Sanskrit scholars, fostering bilingualism and literary learning in court.

scenes.summary: The exiled queen gives birth to prince Konseng among the Nagas, raised in mountain traditions before returning to court.

characters.name: Suhungmung (Swarganarayan)
characters.summary: Expanded the kingdom for the first time since Sukaphaa, annexing Chutia and Dimasa territory and repelling the Bengal invasions of 1527 and 1532–33. First Ahom king to take a Hindu title, Swarganarayan.
characters.notes: Annexed Habung 1512; Chutia kingdom 1523–24; created the Borpatragohain post 1527; killed in his sleep in 1539 by his servant Ratiman.

scenes.title: Konseng's Return and Presentation to King Suhungmung
scenes.summary: Grown into a stalwart warrior, Konseng is brought from the Naga village to Bakata; Suhungmung acknowledges him as half-brother of royal blood.

scenes.title: Creation of the Office of Barpatragohain
scenes.summary: Suhungmung creates a third great ministerial post—the Barpatragohain—elevating Konseng to equal rank with Burhagohain and Borgohain.

scenes.title: Adoption of the Title Swarganarayan and Saka Calendar
scenes.summary: Suhungmung officially assumes the Sanskrit title 'Swarganarayan' (Lord of Heaven), introducing the Saka calendar into state epigraphy.

scenes.title: Suhungmung Orders the First Count of Fighting Men
scenes.summary: Suhungmung orders the first recorded survey of the kingdom's adult men, the base of the later paik militia system.

scenes.title: Ahom Vanguard Marches Against the Chutia Kingdom
scenes.summary: Suhungmung marches an immense land and naval force up the Brahmaputra to confront Chutia monarch Dhirnarayan.

scenes.title: Annexation of the Chutia Kingdom
scenes.summary: Chutia forces routed at Chandangiri; Sadiya annexed into the Ahom Empire; office of Sadiya-Khowa Gohain instituted; firearms and copper-plate treasures acquired.
scenes.notes: Habung was taken in 1512 and Dhirnarayan routed at Dibru in 1523; by 1524 Phrasengmung Borgohain governed Sadiya.

scenes.title: Konseng Fortifies the Western Border
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain deploys stockades, signal towers, and cannon batteries along the western border to counter Bengal Sultanate raids.

scenes.title: Repulse of Early Bengal Sultanate Invasions
scenes.summary: Ahom armies defeat Bengal Sultanate commanders Bit Malik and Mit Manik in naval battles, capturing artillery and cavalry horses.

scenes.title: Ahoms Pursue the Kachari King to Dimapur
scenes.summary: After five years of war, the Kachari king Khunkhara's army is beaten and its commander killed. The Ahoms chase him to his capital Dimapur; he flees, and Suhungmung installs Detsung as Kachari king.
scenes.notes: Khunkhara and Detsung are not yet in the database.

scenes.title: The Great Invasion of Commander Turbak
scenes.summary: General Turbak invades Assam with a large Gaur army armed with muskets, heavy cannons, and cavalry.

scenes.title: Decisive Victory Over Turbak and Pursuit to Karatoya
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain slays Turbak on the battlefield; Bengal forces routed; Ahoms pursue retreating invaders to the sacred Karatoya River.

scenes.title: Foreign Captives Brought Before the Ahom Golden Throne
scenes.summary: Captured enemy generals, cavalry officers, and spoils of war presented before the Swarganarayan in solemn assembly.

scenes.title: Ahom Naval Flotilla River Engagement
scenes.summary: Ahom Bachari war-boats and rowers maneuver against enemy rivercraft with bowmen and bow mounted swivel-guns.

scenes.title: Strategic War Council in the Royal Chamber
scenes.summary: The king and top commanders review maps, troop movements, river currents, and fortress fortifications on the eve of battle.

scenes.title: Mula Gabharu Falls Fighting Turbak
scenes.summary: After her husband Phrasengmung Borgohain is killed by Turbak's army, Princess Mula Gabharu leads women warriors into battle and is killed with five companions. Her death rallies the Ahom army.
scenes.notes: Wikipedia names the Battle of Kachua; much of the story (the Kin Lao vow, her speech) is legend.

scenes.title: Sack of Dimapur and the End of Detsung
scenes.summary: The vassal Kachari king Detsung revolts. The Ahoms pursue him to Jangmarang and kill him; Dimapur is abandoned and the Kacharis move their capital to Maibong. Ahom rule now reaches the Kolong river.
scenes.notes: Detsung is not yet in the database.

scenes.title: Assassination of Suhungmung
scenes.summary: The great king Suhungmung is stabbed in his sleep by his servant Ratiman. His son Suklenmung and a Kachari queen are suspected of the plot.

characters.name: Suklenmung (Garhgayan Roja)
characters.summary: Made Garhgaon the capital and drove the Koch army off the north bank in 1546. In his reign Hari, Sankardev's son-in-law, was executed, leading Sankardev to leave the kingdom.
characters.notes: Some chronicles suspected him in his father's murder.

scenes.title: Accession of Suklenmung
scenes.summary: Suklenmung ascends the throne following Suhungmung's death, establishing Garhgaon as the royal residence.

scenes.title: Assassination of Suhungmung
scenes.summary: The great king Suhungmung is stabbed in his sleep by his servant Ratiman. His son Suklenmung and a Kachari queen are suspected of the plot.

scenes.title: Construction of Fortified Capital Garhgaon and Naga Ali
scenes.summary: Excavates the monumental Garhgaon moat and earthen ramparts, builds brick gateways, and constructs the great Naga Ali military road.

scenes.title: Execution of Hari and Sankardeva Leaves the Ahom Kingdom
scenes.summary: Under Suklenmung, Hari, the son-in-law of the Vaishnava saint Sankardeva, is captured and executed. Sankardeva leaves the Ahom kingdom for Koch territory.
scenes.notes: Sankardeva and Hari are not yet in the database.

scenes.title: Battle of Pichala Against Koch Forces
scenes.summary: Suklenmung defends his kingdom against invading Koch commander Chilarai along the Pichala River, repulsing Koch forces with heavy losses.

scenes.title: Solemn Celebration of the Rikkhvan Ceremony
scenes.summary: Performance of the ancient Tai Rikkhvan ritual to restore royal vitality, longevity, and invincibility in battle.

characters.name: Sukhaamphaa (Khora Roja)
characters.summary: Longest-reigning Ahom king (about 51 years). Chilarai's 1563 invasion forced the Treaty of Majuli. The Ekasarana faith took firm root in his reign.
characters.notes: Nicknamed Khora Roja after a limp from an elephant fall.

scenes.title: Royal Procession of King Sukhaamphaa
scenes.summary: Magnificent procession of Sukhaamphaa riding atop the royal tusker through Garhgaon with gold-embroidered silk standards.

scenes.title: Royal Procession of King Sukhaamphaa
scenes.summary: Magnificent procession of Sukhaamphaa riding atop the royal tusker through Garhgaon with gold-embroidered silk standards.

scenes.title: Chilarai's Invasion of Garhgaon
scenes.summary: Koch king Naranarayan and general Chilarai launch a blitzkrieg; Ahoms execute a tactical retreat into the hills of Namrup.

scenes.title: The Treaty of Majuli
scenes.summary: Peace treaty negotiated on Majuli island; Ahoms cede north bank lands and send royal hostages, enabling subsequent reclamation after Koch departure.

scenes.title: The Long Peace and Cultural Growth Under Khora Raja
scenes.summary: Following early wars, Sukhaamphaa's kingdom experiences prolonged domestic peace, flourishing commerce, and arts.

characters.name: Pratap Singha (Susenghphaa)
characters.summary: Created the Borbarua and Borphukan offices, reorganised the paik system through Momai Tamuli Borbarua, and fought the first Mughal wars.
characters.notes: Also known as Burha Roja and Buddhiswarganarayan. Married Mangaldahi, daughter of Parikshit Narayan, in 1608.

scenes.title: The Golden Forty-Nine-Year Peace of Susenphaa
scenes.summary: One of the longest reigns in Ahom annals; nearly five decades of uninterrupted agricultural and population growth.

scenes.title: Tangshu Naga Raids on Lowland Settlements
scenes.summary: Tangshu Naga warriors raid eastern border villages, looting grain stores and capturing lowland subjects.

scenes.title: Susenphaa's Punitive Tangshu Campaign
scenes.summary: Susenphaa personally leads an army into the rugged Tangshu hills, encircling rebel villages and cutting off mountain passes.

scenes.title: Submission and Tribute of the Tangshu Chiefs
scenes.summary: Defeated Tangshu leaders present offerings of swords, amber, and mountain goods, swearing eternal peace with the Ahom throne.

scenes.title: Erection of Charaideo Boundary Stones
scenes.summary: Inscribed stone monoliths erected around the holy hills of Charaideo to permanently safeguard the royal necropolis.

scenes.title: The Swarganarayan Invests the Royal Commander
scenes.summary: The monarch presents the consecrated Hengdang (royal curved sword) and battle garments to the appointed general.

scenes.title: Ahom Commander Kneels in Fealty Before the King
scenes.summary: A royal commander kneels before the Ahom throne pledging absolute victory or martyrdom for the homeland.

scenes.title: Accession of Susenghphaa (Pratap Singha)
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha ascends the throne at Garhgaon, inaugurating decades of revolutionary governance and resistance against the Mughal Empire.

scenes.title: Accession of Susenghphaa (Pratap Singha)
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha ascends the throne at Garhgaon, inaugurating decades of revolutionary governance and resistance against the Mughal Empire.

scenes.title: Reorganization of the Paik System by Momai Tamuli Barbarua
scenes.summary: Momai Tamuli reorganizes adult males into Paik squads (Gots of 3 or 4 men), mandatory rotation of state labor, and khel guilds, transforming Assam's agrarian and military mobilization.

scenes.title: Pratap Singha Marries the Koch Princess Mangaldoi
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha marries Mangaldoi, daughter of the Koch Hajo king Parikshit Narayan, sealing an alliance against the Mughals.
scenes.notes: Wikipedia spells her name Mangaldahi.

scenes.title: The Jaintia Bride and the Kachari War
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha accepts a Jaintia princess in marriage, but the Kachari king Jasanarayan blocks her passage. War follows; Sundar Gohain drives deep into Kachari land before Bhimbal Konwar's night attack kills him.
scenes.notes: Exact year not found; Jasanarayan, Bhimbal Konwar and Sundar Gohain are not yet in the database.

scenes.title: Balinarayan Takes Refuge at the Ahom Court
scenes.summary: After the Mughals defeat Parikshit of Koch Hajo, his brother Balinarayan flees to Pratap Singha, who makes him tributary raja of Darrang as Dharmanarayan. The refuge angers the Mughal governor Qasim Khan.
scenes.notes: Balinarayan is not yet in the database.

scenes.title: Institution of the Offices of Borbarua and Borphukan
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha creates two supreme executive posts: the Borbarua (prime administrator & chief judicial magistrate) and Borphukan (viceroy & supreme military warden of Lower Assam).

scenes.title: Night Attack at Samdhara: Abu Bakr's Fleet Destroyed
scenes.summary: The first Mughal invasion under Sayyid Abu Bakr and Satrajit takes Kajali, then is destroyed in a night attack by the Bharali–Brahmaputra confluence. Abu Bakr is killed, Satrajit escapes, and Pratap Singha builds a fort at Samdhara inscribed 'Victory in Unequal Battle'.
scenes.notes: Wikipedia dates the Battle of Bharali to 1615 and the Battle of Samdhara to January 1616.

scenes.title: The Mughal War of 1636–1638
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha and Balinarayan push west to Sualkuchi and Hajo. The Mughals under Allah Yar Khan strike back and retake Kamrup; Balinarayan dies, and the Samdhara garrison and the naval fight at Duimunisila stop the Mughal advance.

scenes.title: Treaty of Asurar Ali and Western Defense Line
scenes.summary: Following repeated repulses of Mughal invasions, Pratap Singha signs the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639) with Allah Yar Khan, formalizing the Barnadi River as the frontier.

characters.name: Suramphaa (Jayaditya Singha, Bhoga Roja)
characters.summary: Son of Pratap Singha; deposed in 1644 and later murdered.

character_sheets.caption: Suramphaa portrayed unwell (artistic treatment), grey-background sheet: front, left profile, back, three-quarter, face close-up, right profile, low angle and high angle

scenes.title: Tyranny and Court Intrigue Under Suramphaa
scenes.summary: Suramphaa becomes infatuated with a concubine, disregarding ministers and executing loyal nobles arbitrarily.

scenes.title: Deposition and Poisoning of Suramphaa
scenes.summary: The council of ministers deposes the tyrannical king and removes him from power.

characters.name: Sutingphaa (Noriya Roja)
characters.summary: Brother of Suramphaa; deposed by the Burhagohain in 1648 and later murdered.

scenes.title: The Frail Reign of Sutingphaa
scenes.summary: Afflicted by chronic disease and goitre, Sutingphaa struggles to rule while court factions vie for supremacy.

scenes.title: Prince Sutamla Organizes Court Loyalists
scenes.summary: Prince Sutamla rallies ministers and soldiers to remove his incapacitated father to restore imperial governance.

characters.name: Jayadhwaj Singha (Sutamla)
characters.summary: Drove the Mughals from Guwahati in 1648. Mir Jumla took Garhgaon in March 1662; the king withdrew to Namrup and signed the Treaty of Ghilajharighat in January 1663. A patron of Vaishnava satras.
characters.notes: Called Bhagania Roja (“the fugitive”). Struck the first coins in his name.

scenes.title: Prince Sutamla Organizes Court Loyalists
scenes.summary: Prince Sutamla rallies ministers and soldiers to remove his incapacitated father to restore imperial governance.

scenes.title: Coronation of Jayadhwaj Singha
scenes.summary: Sutamla ascends the throne taking the regal Hindu name Jayadhwaj Singha, the first Ahom monarch to issue coins with Sanskrit inscriptions.

scenes.title: Solemn Vigil at the Royal Deathbed
scenes.summary: Court ministers, priests, and queens maintain vigil around the royal bed chamber as a Swargadeo departs for the realm of ancestors.

scenes.title: Adoption of Hindu Rituals in Sutamla's Court
scenes.summary: Sutamla formalizes Hindu court rituals, patronizing Vaishnava monasteries and adopting Sanskrit titulature alongside Tai liturgy.

scenes.title: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma
scenes.summary: Jayadhwaj takes spiritual initiation from Niranjan Bapu of Auniati Satra, formally adopting Mahapuruxiya Ekasarana Dharma as royal faith.

scenes.title: Royal Initiation into Ekasarana Dharma
scenes.summary: Jayadhwaj takes spiritual initiation from Niranjan Bapu of Auniati Satra, formally adopting Mahapuruxiya Ekasarana Dharma as royal faith.

scenes.title: The First Ahom Coins Are Struck
scenes.summary: Coins first appear under Jayadhwaj Singha. The old belief that Suklenmung struck the first Ahom coins comes from misread coins of Chakradhwaj Singha.

scenes.title: Jayadhwaj Singha Takes Guwahati
scenes.summary: While Shah Jahan's sons fight for the Mughal throne, the Mughal faujdar abandons Guwahati. Jayadhwaj Singha's army occupies Kamrup and pushes the Koch king Pran Narayan back beyond Dhubri. This is the direct cause of Mir Jumla's invasion.
scenes.notes: Sources disagree whether the Koches or the Ahoms entered Guwahati first.

scenes.title: Royal Naam-Prasanga and Satra Endowments
scenes.summary: The king participates in choral chanting (Naam-Prasanga) and donates extensive rent-free lands and paiks to the satras of Majuli.

scenes.title: Mir Jumla's Imperial Mughal Invasion
scenes.summary: Aurangzeb's premier general and Viceroy of Bengal, Mir Jumla, advances up the Brahmaputra with 12,000 cavalry, 30,000 infantry, and 323 armed war boats.

scenes.title: Mughal Capture of Capital Garhgaon
scenes.summary: Mir Jumla enters Garhgaon in victory; thousands of Ahom cannons, gold treasures, and grain reserves are captured by imperial Mughal forces.

scenes.title: The Monsoon Counter-War of Namrup
scenes.summary: From hills of Namrup, Jayadhwaj unleashes guerrilla warfare during torrential monsoons, severing Mughal supply lines and decimating Mir Jumla's trapped army with epidemic fever.

scenes.title: The Treaty of Ghilajharighat
scenes.summary: Severely ill Mir Jumla and exhausted Jayadhwaj sign treaty; Ahoms cede Western Assam, pay war indemnities of gold, silver, 90 elephants, and send princesses.

scenes.title: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
scenes.summary: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

scenes.title: Departure of Princess Ramani Gabharu to Delhi
scenes.summary: Six-year-old Princess Ramani Gabharu (daughter of Jayadhwaj) is tearfully handed over as part of the treaty to be sent to Delhi, where she later marries Prince Azam Shah as Rahmat Banu Begum.

scenes.title: King Jayadhwaj Singha's Vow of Liberation
scenes.summary: Brokenhearted by the humiliating treaty and daughter's departure, Jayadhwaj returns to ruined Garhgaon and urges the court never to rest until the Mughals are expelled.

scenes.title: Deathbed of King Jayadhwaj Singha
scenes.summary: On his deathbed at Bakata, Jayadhwaj extracts a solemn oath from his successor Chakradhwaj Singha to wipe out the shame of Mughal conquest.

characters.name: Chakradhwaj Singha (Supangmung)
characters.summary: Refused Mughal tribute, rebuilt the army and recaptured Guwahati in 1667. Appointed Atan Burhagohain Rajmantri Dangaria and Lachit Borphukan commander.
characters.notes: Died April 1670.

scenes.title: Chakradhwaj Singha's Oath of Resistance
scenes.summary: Receiving a patronizing Mughal royal robe (khilat) from Delhi, King Chakradhwaj angrily throws it down, proclaiming: 'Death is preferable to a state of subordination to the Bengas!'

scenes.title: Lachit Tested and Appointed Supreme Commander
scenes.summary: Chakradhwaj tests Lachit's presence of mind with a staged court insult; impressed by his fierce dignity, the king confers the golden sword and supreme command of the army to liberate Guwahati.

scenes.title: Lachit Borphukan Liberates Guwahati
scenes.summary: Ahom forces execute a coordinated amphibious night assault, breaching the Mughal ramparts and driving imperial troops out of Guwahati.

scenes.title: Recapture of the Strategic Fort of Itakhuli
scenes.summary: Lachit storm-attacks the strategic Itakhuli fortress, capturing vast Mughal artillery, war sloops, and driving imperial forces beyond the Manas.

scenes.title: The Tragic Battle of Alaboi
scenes.summary: Compelled by Chakradhwaj to engage Ram Singh's cavalry on open plains, 10,000 Ahom braves perish in a single day; Lachit weeps bitterly for his fallen soldiers.

scenes.title: Total Military Reorganization After Alaboi
scenes.summary: Chakradhwaj and Lachit regroup, constructing massive defensive mud ramparts (Gars) around Saraighat and converting strategy to pure riverine warfare.

characters.summary: Brother of Chakradhwaj; renewed the war with the Mughals and ordered Lachit to Saraighat. Deposed and executed.

scenes.summary: Upon succeeding Chakradhwaj, Udayaditya reaffirms complete faith in Lachit Borphukan, coordinating logistics for the impending Mughal clash.

scenes.title: Fortification of Saraighat and Execution of the Negligent Uncle
scenes.summary: Lachit oversees construction of the Saraighat earthen rampart overnight; finding his maternal uncle negligent, he beheads him uttering: 'My uncle is not greater than my country!'

scenes.title: Lachit Rallies Retreating Troops from His Sickbed
scenes.summary: Suffering from severe high fever, Lachit orders his sickbed carried onto his royal war-boat, shouting to retreating soldiers: 'If you wish to flee, do so! But let the King know I died fighting!'

scenes.title: The Epic Naval Battle of Saraighat
scenes.summary: Ahom fleet traps Ram Singh's Mughal armada at the narrowest gorge of the Brahmaputra at Saraighat; Mughal naval force is completely shattered in a historic tactical masterpiece.

scenes.summary: Expedition launched to pacify Dafla hillmen raiding north bank villages; harsh conditions test the royal army.

scenes.title: Death of Lachit Borphukan at Kaliabor
scenes.summary: About a year after Saraighat, Lachit Borphukan dies of illness at Kaliabor. Udayaditya Singha builds the Lachit Maidam at Hoolungapara and makes Lachit's brother Laluk Sola the new Borphukan.
scenes.notes: Death date given as 25 April 1672 in some sources.

scenes.title: Palace Coup Against Udayaditya Singha
scenes.summary: Angered by the king's devotion to the ascetic Paramananda Sanyasi and his jailing of Vaishnava mahantas, Debera Hazarika and the king's brother Sarugohain storm the palace at midnight. Udayaditya is taken to Charaideo and killed; his brother takes the throne as Ramdhwaj Singha.
scenes.notes: Paramananda Sanyasi is not yet in the database.

scenes.title: Gobar Raja Crowned as Debera's Puppet
scenes.summary: Debera crowns Tungkhungia prince Gobar (father of Gadadhar Singha) as king to maintain his puppet grip over the throne.

scenes.title: Atan Burhagohain Captures Garhgaon and Executes Debera and Gobar
scenes.summary: Atan Burhagohain leads an army of loyalist commanders from Guwahati to Garhgaon, arrests and executes Debera and deposes Gobar.

characters.name: Sujinphaa (Arjun Konwar)
characters.summary: Grandson of Pratap Singha, installed by Atan Burhagohain; deposed and died by suicide.

scenes.title: Installation of Sujinphaa by Atan Burhagohain
scenes.summary: Noble statesman Atan Burhagohain refuses the crown himself and adheres strictly to constitution by placing Dihingia prince Sujinphaa on the throne.

scenes.title: Court Suspicion and Rift Between King and Premier
scenes.summary: Influenced by plotting sons and courtiers, Sujinphaa begins to view the immensely popular Atan Burhagohain with bitter suspicion.

scenes.title: The Royal Army Deserts Sujinphaa
scenes.summary: When Sujinphaa attempts an armed ambush against the Burhagohain, royal soldiers refuse to strike their beloved prime minister and desert the king.

scenes.title: Deposition and Tragic End of Sujinphaa
scenes.summary: Sujinphaa is captured, blinded according to Ahom dynastic custom, and passes away in confinement.

scenes.title: Accession and Court of Sudoiphaa Paratiya Raja
scenes.summary: Paratiya prince ascends the throne; kingdom faces external intrigue from Lower Assam viceroy Laluk Sola Borphukan.

scenes.title: Treason of Laluk Sola: Surrender of Guwahati to the Mughals
scenes.summary: In an act of monstrous betrayal, Laluk Sola Borphukan surrenders Guwahati to Mughal Prince Azam Tara for 400,000 rupees and promises of being made Raja.

characters.name: Sulikphaa (Ratnadhwaj Singha, Lora Roja)
characters.summary: A boy king under Laluk Sola Borphukan; deposed and killed. A rule that claimants must be physically unblemished was introduced in his reign.

scenes.title: Prince Gadapani Escapes into the Hills in Disguise
scenes.summary: Forewarned by his courageous wife Joymoti, tall and muscular Prince Gadapani flees in disguise into the Naga hills to evade royal executioners.

scenes.title: Installation of the Teenaged Boy-King Sulikphaa
scenes.summary: Laluk Sola murders Atan Burhagohain and crowns 14-year-old Sulikphaa (Lora Raja) to govern through terror and usurp power.

scenes.title: The Great Purge and Mutilation of Royal Princes
scenes.summary: Laluk Sola and Sulikphaa unleash death squads across Assam to kill, blind, or slit the ears of all eligible Ahom princes to disqualify them from the throne.

scenes.title: Martyrdom of Princess Joymoti Konwari
scenes.summary: Tied to thorn bushes on Jerenga Pathar and brutally tortured for 14 continuous days by Lora Raja's agents, Princess Joymoti breathes her last refusing to betray her husband Gadapani.

scenes.title: Murder of Laluk Sola Borphukan
scenes.summary: The Borphukan who sold Guwahati to the Mughals is killed by his own bodyguard, ending his hold over the boy-king Sulikphaa.

characters.name: Gadadhar Singha (Supaatphaa)
characters.summary: Founder of the Tungkhungia line. Came out of exile in the Naga hills to take the throne in 1681 and retook Guwahati at Itakhuli in 1682, ending the Ahom–Mughal wars.
characters.notes: Husband of Joymoti Konwari. Built the Dhodar Ali road and began a land survey.
characters.relation: Son of Gobar Roja; first Tungkhungia king

scenes.title: Martyrdom of Princess Joymoti Konwari
scenes.summary: Tied to thorn bushes on Jerenga Pathar and brutally tortured for 14 continuous days by Lora Raja's agents, Princess Joymoti breathes her last refusing to betray her husband Gadapani.

scenes.title: Gadadhar Singha Takes the Throne and Marshals the Army
scenes.summary: Overthrowing Lora Raja, Gadadhar Singha mobilizes the kingdom's armed forces to permanently purge Assam of Mughal occupation.

scenes.title: Battle of Itakhuli: The Mughals Driven to the Manas
scenes.summary: Gadadhar Singha's three-pronged army and navy close on Guwahati. After the naval battle at Paniduar on 15 August, the Itakhuli fort falls and the Mughals are chased to the Manas river, which becomes the accepted border. The Ahom–Mughal wars end.

scenes.title: Imperial Conference with Vaishnava Satradhikars
scenes.summary: King Gadadhar Singha meets with powerful abbots (Satradhikars), asserting absolute royal authority over monastic wealth and exempt paiks.

scenes.title: Royal Visitation to the Satra Naamghar
scenes.summary: The austere Swargadeo visits a monastic prayer hall (Naamghar) to ensure monastic orders do not undermine state military recruitment.

scenes.title: Gadadhar Singha's Persecution of the Satras
scenes.summary: Late in his reign Gadadhar Singha turns on the Vaishnava satras. The Dakhinpat gosain is mutilated and his idols melted down, the Auniati head flees, and Mayamara disciples suffer most. The grievance feeds the later Moamoria rebellion.
scenes.notes: Motives (personal grudge or politico-economic) are debated.

characters.name: Rudra Singha (Sukhrungphaa)
characters.summary: Took the kingdom to its peak, founded Rangpur as the capital, campaigned against the Dimasa and Jaintia kingdoms (1706–08) and planned a great war on Mughal Bengal, dying before it began.
characters.notes: Born c. 1665; died 27 August 1714 at North Guwahati.

scenes.summary: Son of Joymoti and Gadadhar Singha ascends the throne; initiates the zenith of Ahom political grandeur, architecture, and international diplomacy.

scenes.title: Rangnath Dol and the Namdang Stone Bridge
scenes.summary: Rudra Singha builds the Rangnath Dol and the Namdang stone bridge, cut from a single rock, followed by the Fakuwa Dol in 1703–04.

scenes.title: King Rudra Singha Inaugurates Royal Festivities at Rang Ghar
scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides over Rongali Bihu festivities, buffalo fights, elephant encounters, and folk dances from the royal pavilion at Rang Ghar.

scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides over Rongali Bihu festivities, buffalo fights, elephant encounters, and folk dances from the royal pavilion at Rang Ghar.

scenes.title: Subjugation and Vassalage of the Kachari and Jaintia Rulers
scenes.summary: Following victorious campaigns, Rudra Singha receives envoys and rulers of the Kacharis and Jaintias who submit tribute and acknowledge Ahom supremacy.

scenes.title: Grand Durbar and the Seven-Tiered Singhason at Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides from the legendary jewel-inlaid lion throne (Singhason) under a golden canopy, welcoming foreign envoys from all corners of India.

scenes.summary: Rudra Singha presides from the legendary jewel-inlaid lion throne (Singhason) under a golden canopy, welcoming foreign envoys from all corners of India.

scenes.title: Rudra Singha Plans the Invasion of Bengal
scenes.summary: At a general assembly at Rangpur, Rudra Singha announces his plan to invade Mughal Bengal with a league of Hindu rajas, and moves his army to Guwahati.

scenes.title: Death of Rudra Singha at the Guwahati Camp
scenes.summary: Eight days after falling ill, Rudra Singha dies in camp at Guwahati with the Bengal campaign unlaunched. On his deathbed he tells his son Siva Singha to take Krishnaram Bhattacharya as guru.

characters.name: Siva Singha (Sutanphaa)
characters.summary: A devout Shakta who gave land to temples and Brahmins and shared royal authority with his queens, who ruled in turn as Bar Raja. A golden age of Assamese manuscripts.

character_sheets.caption: Siva Singha (Sutanphaa), scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: Death of Rudra Singha at the Guwahati Camp
scenes.summary: Eight days after falling ill, Rudra Singha dies in camp at Guwahati with the Bengal campaign unlaunched. On his deathbed he tells his son Siva Singha to take Krishnaram Bhattacharya as guru.

scenes.title: Krishnaram Bhattacharya Becomes the Parbatiya Gosain
scenes.summary: Siva Singha becomes the disciple of the Nabadwip Shakta priest Krishnaram Bhattacharya and gives him charge of the Kamakhya temple on Nilachal hill, where he is known as the Parbatiya Gosain.

scenes.title: Transfer of Royal Power to Queen Phuleswari (Bar Raja)
scenes.summary: Panicked by astrological predictions of Chhatra-bhanga (loss of kingship), Siva Singha transfers the sovereign umbrella, royal seal, and rule to his chief queen Phuleswari.

scenes.title: Excavation of Gaurisagar Tank and Temples
scenes.summary: Queen Phuleswari excavates Gaurisagar tank and erects temples dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Devi along its banks.

scenes.title: Queen Phuleswari's Persecution of Moamoria Vaishnavas
scenes.summary: Queen Phuleswari aggressively enforces Shakta worship, compelling Moamoria Vaishnavite Mahantas to smear sacrificial animal blood on their foreheads, igniting decades of bitter hatred.

scenes.title: Construction of Sivasagar Tank (Bor Pukhuri) and Shiva Dol
scenes.summary: Queen Ambika excavates the monumental 257-acre Sivasagar tank and erects the 104-foot-high Shiva Dol, one of India's tallest stone temple shikhara towers.

scenes.title: Painting of the Hastividyarnava
scenes.summary: Under Siva Singha and Queen Ambika, Sukumar Barkaith writes the Hastividyarnava, a treatise on royal elephants, illustrated by the painters Dilbar and Dosai.
scenes.notes: Sukumar Barkaith, Dilbar and Dosai are not yet in the database.

scenes.title: The Great Cadastral Land Survey (Pek-Kakar)
scenes.summary: Comprehensive statewide land measurement and census of households and cultivation acreage conducted across Assam.

scenes.title: Sarbeswari Becomes the Third Bar Raja
scenes.summary: After Ambika's death, Siva Singha raises another queen to rule as Bar Raja under the name Sarbeswari; she holds the title until his death in 1744.
scenes.notes: Sources differ on her earlier name (Akari Gabharu or Enadari).

characters.name: Pramatta Singha (Sunenphaa)
characters.summary: Brother of Siva Singha; died naturally. Catalogued scenes show Rang Ghar games in his reign.

character_sheets.caption: Pramatta Singha (Sunenphaa), scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: Construction and Dedication of the Masonry Rang Ghar
scenes.summary: Pramatta Singha reconstructs Rang Ghar in permanent fired brick and egg-mortar as a magnificent two-storied oval sports colosseum.

scenes.title: Royal Buffalo Fights on Rupahi Pathar
scenes.summary: The King and royal court watch thrilling buffalo fights, bird duels, and martial acrobatics held in the arena beneath the pavilion arches.

scenes.title: Royal Court Assembly at the Rang Ghar Pavilion
scenes.summary: Aristocratic gathering of Gohains, royal ladies, and vassal chiefs on the terrace of Rang Ghar during spring festivities.

scenes.title: Kirti Chandra Borbarua Crowns Rajeswar Singha
scenes.summary: On Pramatta Singha's death, the Borbarua Kirti Chandra passes over the elder princes and places Rajeswar Singha on the throne, beginning two decades of his dominance at court.

characters.name: Rajeswar Singha (Suremphaa)
characters.summary: Fourth son of Rudra Singha. Sheltered Bhagyachandra of Manipur, sent the failed 1765 expedition, and married Kuranganayani in 1768. Much of the governing fell to Kirti Chandra Borbarua.
characters.notes: Died at Dergaon in 1769. Added three underground storeys to the Kareng Ghar (Talatal Ghar).

character_sheets.caption: Rajeswar Singha (Suremphaa), scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: Expansion of the Grand Talatal Ghar Palace
scenes.summary: Rajeswar Singha expands Talatal Ghar into a 7-storied architectural wonder (4 above ground, 3 underground) equipped with secret evacuation tunnels to Dikhou river.

scenes.title: Kirti Chandra Borbarua Crowns Rajeswar Singha
scenes.summary: On Pramatta Singha's death, the Borbarua Kirti Chandra passes over the elder princes and places Rajeswar Singha on the throne, beginning two decades of his dominance at court.

scenes.title: Rebuilding the Kareng Ghar at Garhgaon
scenes.summary: Rajeswar Singha replaces the wooden palace at Garhgaon with the brick and stone seven-storey Kareng Ghar that still stands.
scenes.notes: The Kareng Ghar infobox gives 1758; the text and the Sivasagar district site give 1752.

scenes.title: The Burning of the Buranjis
scenes.summary: Stung by the Chakari-pheti Buranji's mockery of his low birth, Kirti Chandra Borbarua has the Buranjis collected and burns those he judges false. Some copies survive.
scenes.notes: Most sources place this under Rajeswar Singha; some under Lakshmi Singha. Numali Borgohain (author of the Chakari-pheti) is not yet in the database.

scenes.title: Lata-Katai Ran: The Mountain Expedition to Manipur
scenes.summary: Rajeswar Singha dispatches an army across trackless, creepers-choked mountain jungles ('Lata-Katai Ran') to liberate Manipur from Burmese occupation and reinstate Meitei King Jai Singh.

scenes.title: Royal Wedding of Rajeswar Singha and Princess Kuranganayani
scenes.summary: In gratitude, King Jai Singh gives his heroic daughter Princess Kuranganayani in marriage to Rajeswar Singha, cementing eternal Ahom-Manipuri ties.

characters.name: Lakshmi Singha (Sunyeophaa)
characters.summary: Made king by Kirti Chandra Borbarua. The Moamoria rebellion began in 1769 and the rebels captured him; royalists restored him in 1770.
characters.notes: Died 13 December 1780.

character_sheets.caption: Lakshmi Singha (Sunyeophaa), scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Moamoria Rebellion
scenes.summary: Enraged by insults to their Guru, peasant masses and Moran disciples of the Moamoria Satra revolt, routing royal forces and capturing the capital Rangpur.

scenes.title: Captivity and Imprisonment of King Lakshmi Singha
scenes.summary: Rebels capture Swargadeo Lakshmi Singha, imprison him at the Joysagar temple, and declare Ramakanta as ruler and Ragha Moran as Barbarua.

scenes.title: Queen Kuranganayani's Daring Counter-Coup
scenes.summary: During Rongali Bihu, Queen Kuranganayani bravely strikes down the usurper Ragha Moran with a sword blow from behind; loyalist nobles storm the palace and liberate King Lakshmi Singha.

scenes.title: Royal Retribution and Repression of Moamoria Rebels
scenes.summary: Restored royal government executes thousands of Moamoria adherents and leaders, cementing irreversible societal rifts.

characters.name: Gaurinath Singha (Suhitpangphaa)
characters.summary: Became king at about fifteen. Rebels took the capital in 1786; British troops under Captain Welsh restored order in lower Assam in 1792–94 and then left. Died at Jorhat in December 1794.
characters.notes: The infobox gives 1794 as the end; the king list gives 1795.

character_sheets.caption: Gaurinath Singha (Suhitpangphaa), scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: The Bihu Ambush on Gaurinath Singha
scenes.summary: During Bohag Bihu the Moamorias attack the convoy of the newly crowned Gaurinath Singha. He escapes; the rebels briefly take Rangpur before Ghanashyam Burhagohain retakes it, followed by mass killings.

scenes.title: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

scenes.title: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

scenes.title: Flight of King Gaurinath Singha Down the Brahmaputra
scenes.summary: Swargadeo Gaurinath flees in despair from burning Upper Assam on royal barges to take refuge in Guwahati.

scenes.title: Bharat Singha Crowned at Rangpur
scenes.summary: With Gaurinath in exile at Guwahati, the Moamorias install Bharat Singha as king at Rangpur. He strikes coins claiming descent from Bhagadatta, and is killed in 1799.
scenes.notes: Coins in his name are dated 1789–94 and 1796–97.

scenes.title: British Military Intervention: Captain Thomas Welsh Expedition
scenes.summary: Responding to Gaurinath's appeal, British East India Company sends 6 companies of sepoys under Captain Thomas Welsh who defeat rebels and re-enter Rangpur.

scenes.title: The Ahom-British Commercial Treaty of 1793
scenes.summary: First formal commercial agreement signed between Ahom monarchy and the British East India Company, regulating customs and trade between Bengal and Assam.

scenes.title: The Capital Moves from Rangpur to Jorhat
scenes.summary: With Rangpur wrecked by the rebellion, the Ahom court moves its capital to Jorhat, which stays the last capital of the kingdom.
scenes.notes: Sources disagree on whether the move was completed before or after Gaurinath's death.

characters.name: Kamaleswar Singha (Suklingphaa)
characters.summary: Placed on the throne as an infant by Purnananda Burhagohain, who held real power; died of smallpox.

character_sheets.caption: Kamaleswar Singha (Suklingphaa), scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: The Autocratic Regency of Premier Purnananda Burhagohain
scenes.summary: Purnananda Burhagohain exercises de facto sovereign rule, establishing Jorhat as new capital, drilling troops with modern British flintlocks, and suppressing insurrections.

characters.name: Chandrakanta Singha (Sudingphaa)
characters.summary: Named king at about fourteen by Purnananda Burhagohain. Deposed in 1818, reinstalled by the Burmese in 1819, defeated in 1822 and fled to British territory. Died in Guwahati in 1839.
characters.notes: Born c. 1797. After Yandabo he received a pension of 500 rupees.

character_sheets.caption: Chandrakanta Singha (Sudingphaa), scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: Deadly Court Factionalism Between Burhagohain and Borphukan
scenes.summary: Young Chandrakanta Singha sides with favorite Satram against the elderly Purnananda; Badan Chandra Borphukan conspires against the premier.

scenes.title: The First Burmese Invasion (Manor Din Begins)
scenes.summary: Badan Chandra brings a Burmese army of 16,000 soldiers across the Patkai; Purnananda dies of heartbreak; Burmese defeat Ahom troops at Ghiladhari and march on Jorhat.

scenes.title: The First Burmese Invasion (Manor Din Begins)
scenes.summary: Badan Chandra brings a Burmese army of 16,000 soldiers across the Patkai; Purnananda dies of heartbreak; Burmese defeat Ahom troops at Ghiladhari and march on Jorhat.

scenes.title: Assassination of Traitor Badan Chandra Borphukan
scenes.summary: Subedar Rup Singh strikes down Badan Chandra Borphukan with a dao while bathing in Jorhat, executing retribution for bringing Burmese invaders.

scenes.title: Deposition of Chandrakanta and Accession of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Ruchinath Burhagohain captures Jorhat, slits Chandrakanta's right ear to permanently disqualify him from kingship, and crowns Purandar Singha.

scenes.title: Restoration of Chandrakanta Singha as Burmese Puppet
scenes.summary: Burmese restore ear-mutilated Chandrakanta to the throne, but Burmese generals retain real power.

scenes.title: Chandrakanta's Resistance and Flight from Burmese Reign of Terror
scenes.summary: When Burmese attempt to murder him, Chandrakanta flees to British frontier and organizes armed resistance against Burmese pillagers.

scenes.title: Chandrakanta Retakes Guwahati
scenes.summary: Raising troops in British territory, Chandrakanta Singha recaptures Assam Chowki in October and Guwahati in December 1821.

scenes.title: Chandrakanta's Last Stand at Mahgarh
scenes.summary: Chandrakanta camps at Mahgarh near Jorhat. Maha Bandula's Burmese army defeats him in April 1822 and he falls back to Guwahati.

scenes.title: Defeat at Hadira Chowki; Tilwa Proclaimed Raja of Assam
scenes.summary: Mingimaha Tilwa defeats Chandrakanta at Hadira (Assam) Chowki. Chandrakanta withdraws to British territory, and Tilwa is declared Raja of Assam, ending Ahom rule until 1826.
scenes.notes: Wikipedia places the defeat in June 1822, with an alternative account in July.

characters.name: Purandar Singha
characters.summary: Installed as a boy in 1818 by Ruchinath Burhagohain, lost the throne to the Burmese in 1819, and was made a tributary prince by the British in 1833. Deposed in September 1838.
characters.notes: Born 1807, died 1 October 1846 at Jorhat. Also called Suremphaa II.

character_sheets.caption: Purandar Singha, scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: Deposition of Chandrakanta and Accession of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Ruchinath Burhagohain captures Jorhat, slits Chandrakanta's right ear to permanently disqualify him from kingship, and crowns Purandar Singha.

scenes.title: Second Burmese Invasion and Flight of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Burmese monarch sends large army under Ala Mingi; Purandar and Ruchinath are routed at Nazira and flee into British Bengal territory.

scenes.title: Restoration of Purandar Singha as Protected Tributary Ruler
scenes.summary: British East India Company reinstates Purandar Singha over Upper Assam conditioned on paying an impossible annual tribute of 50,000 Company rupees.

scenes.title: Crushing Tax Demands on War-Devastated Population
scenes.summary: Purandar struggles desperately to collect taxes from a depopulated and ruined citizenry to satisfy the exorbitant British tribute demand.

scenes.title: Crushing Tax Demands on War-Devastated Population
scenes.summary: Purandar struggles desperately to collect taxes from a depopulated and ruined citizenry to satisfy the exorbitant British tribute demand.

scenes.title: Final British Annexation of Assam and Deposition of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Accusing him of default and misgovernment, the British formally depose Purandar Singha, annexing Upper Assam into the British Empire and ending the Ahom dynasty forever.

characters.name: Jogeswar Singha
characters.summary: A puppet king installed by the Burmese commander Mingimaha Tilwa in 1821; removed in 1822.

character_sheets.caption: Jogeswar Singha, scene-based illustrated reconstruction, grey-background eight-view character sheet

scenes.title: Burmese Atrocities (Manor Din) Under Puppet Jogeswar Singha
scenes.summary: Burmese install powerless puppet Jogeswar Singha while massacring tens of thousands of Assamese civilians, depopulating entire districts.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Anglo-Burmese War in Assam
scenes.summary: British East India Company declares war on Burma; British regiments and gunboats advance up the Brahmaputra, expelling Burmese forces.

scenes.title: Expulsion of the Burmese from Upper Assam
scenes.summary: Colonel Richards defeats and forces surrender of the Burmese garrison at Rangpur stockade in January 1825.

scenes.title: Signing of the Historic Treaty of Yandabo
scenes.summary: The King of Ava formally cedes all claims to Assam to the British East India Company, terminating 598 years of independent Ahom rule.

characters.summary: Daughter of the Kamata king (Kamateswar), given with her sister Bhajani to Sukhaangphaa to seal a truce. Mother of Sukhrangphaa, Sutuphaa, Tyao Khamti and Tyao Chulai.

scenes.summary: Peace concluded by the marriage of Kamata Princess Rajani (Durlabhanarayana's daughter) to Sukhangphaa, sealing durable inter-kingdom peace.

scenes.summary: Princess Rajani gives birth to Prince Chao Pulai, tying the royal lineages of Kamata and Ahom together.

scenes.summary: Princess Rajani gives birth to Prince Chao Pulai, tying the royal lineages of Kamata and Ahom together.

scenes.title: Chao Pulai's Revolt and Alliance with Kamata
scenes.summary: Chao Pulai disputes the succession of his half-brother Sukhrangphaa and conspires with maternal Kamata envoys for military support.

scenes.title: Fraternal Reconciliation Between Sukhrangphaa and Chao Pulai
scenes.summary: Rather than shedding fraternal blood, Sukhrangphaa welcomes Chao Pulai back into the court and effects complete reconciliation.

scenes.title: Appointment of Chao Pulai as Governor of Sadiya
scenes.summary: King Sukhrangphaa invests Chao Pulai with governorship of the critical eastern frontier outpost of Sadiya.

characters.name: Tai Sulai
characters.summary: A rival claimant to the Ahom throne who fled to Mungkang and gained an invasion force; Sudangphaa defeated it and the 1401 treaty fixed the Patkai boundary.

scenes.title: Sudangphaa Repels the Mong Kawng Invasion
scenes.summary: The rival claimant Tai Sulai returns with a Mong Kawng (Mungkang) army led by the defector Tasim Pou. Sudangphaa meets it near Kuhiarbari in the Tipam country and defeats it, though he is lightly wounded by a spear.
scenes.notes: Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive.

scenes.title: Nangchukham Borgohain Marches on Kamata
scenes.summary: Tai Sulai flees to Kamata. Sudangphaa's commander Nangchukham Borgohain invades, and the Kamata king, also pressed by Bengal, makes peace and gives a daughter in marriage to Sudangphaa.
scenes.notes: Chronology of the Kamata episode is undated and disputed. Modern artistic reconstruction using project character sheets; setting, architecture and staging are interpretive.

characters.name: Mula Gabharu (Nang Mula)
characters.summary: Wife of Ahom commander Phrasengmung Borgohain, remembered for joining the resistance against Turbak in 1532.

scenes.title: Mula Gabharu Falls Fighting Turbak
scenes.summary: After her husband Phrasengmung Borgohain is killed by Turbak's army, Princess Mula Gabharu leads women warriors into battle and is killed with five companions. Her death rallies the Ahom army.
scenes.notes: Wikipedia names the Battle of Kachua; much of the story (the Kin Lao vow, her speech) is legend.

scenes.summary: Pratap Singha marries Mangaldoi, daughter of the Koch Hajo king Parikshit Narayan, sealing an alliance against the Mughals.

scenes.title: Prince Gadapani Escapes into the Hills in Disguise
scenes.summary: Forewarned by his courageous wife Joymoti, tall and muscular Prince Gadapani flees in disguise into the Naga hills to evade royal executioners.

scenes.title: Martyrdom of Princess Joymoti Konwari
scenes.summary: Tied to thorn bushes on Jerenga Pathar and brutally tortured for 14 continuous days by Lora Raja's agents, Princess Joymoti breathes her last refusing to betray her husband Gadapani.

characters.name: Phuleswari (Pramatheswari)
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: A dancer of the Nat caste made Bar Raja under Siva Singha after astrologers predicted the king's fall. Minted coins in joint names and pressed to make Shaktism the state religion; died in 1731 in childbirth.
characters.notes: Her insult to the Moamoria Gosains is cited as a cause of the later rebellion.

character_sheets.caption: Phuleswari (Pramatheswari), eight-view artistic reconstruction remade from user clothing references: elongated face, high braided bun, gold jacket and crimson borders. Costume and appearance are interpretive.

scenes.title: Transfer of Royal Power to Queen Phuleswari (Bar Raja)
scenes.summary: Panicked by astrological predictions of Chhatra-bhanga (loss of kingship), Siva Singha transfers the sovereign umbrella, royal seal, and rule to his chief queen Phuleswari.

scenes.title: Excavation of Gaurisagar Tank and Temples
scenes.summary: Queen Phuleswari excavates Gaurisagar tank and erects temples dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Devi along its banks.

scenes.title: Queen Phuleswari's Persecution of Moamoria Vaishnavas
scenes.summary: Queen Phuleswari aggressively enforces Shakta worship, compelling Moamoria Vaishnavite Mahantas to smear sacrificial animal blood on their foreheads, igniting decades of bitter hatred.

characters.name: Ambika
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: Phuleswari's sister. Sponsored the Hastividyarnava and the Sivasagar Siva Doul.
characters.notes: Sources give her death as 1738 or the end of her reign as 1739.

character_sheets.caption: Ambika, eight-view artistic reconstruction remade from user clothing references: rounded face, low bun, ivory jacket and purple woven motifs. Costume and appearance are interpretive.

scenes.title: Construction of Sivasagar Tank (Bor Pukhuri) and Shiva Dol
scenes.summary: Queen Ambika excavates the monumental 257-acre Sivasagar tank and erects the 104-foot-high Shiva Dol, one of India's tallest stone temple shikhara towers.

scenes.title: Painting of the Hastividyarnava
scenes.summary: Under Siva Singha and Queen Ambika, Sukumar Barkaith writes the Hastividyarnava, a treatise on royal elephants, illustrated by the painters Dilbar and Dosai.
scenes.notes: Sukumar Barkaith, Dilbar and Dosai are not yet in the database.

characters.name: Sarbeswari (Endari)
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: Held the same authority as her predecessors but was less active in patronising Shaktism.

character_sheets.caption: Sarbeswari (Endari), eight-view artistic reconstruction remade from user clothing references: angular face, double-rosette headdress, gold jacket and red patterned wrap. Costume and appearance are interpretive.

scenes.title: Sarbeswari Becomes the Third Bar Raja
scenes.summary: After Ambika's death, Siva Singha raises another queen to rule as Bar Raja under the name Sarbeswari; she holds the title until his death in 1744.
scenes.notes: Sources differ on her earlier name (Akari Gabharu or Enadari).

characters.role: Manipuri princess, queen of the Ahom kingdom
characters.summary: Married Rajeswar Singha in 1768 as thanks for Ahom help to her father. After his death she was taken by the rebel Ragha Moran and helped bring about his killing in April 1770; she later married Lakshmi Singha.

scenes.title: Royal Wedding of Rajeswar Singha and Princess Kuranganayani
scenes.summary: In gratitude, King Jai Singh gives his heroic daughter Princess Kuranganayani in marriage to Rajeswar Singha, cementing eternal Ahom-Manipuri ties.

scenes.title: Queen Kuranganayani's Daring Counter-Coup
scenes.summary: During Rongali Bihu, Queen Kuranganayani bravely strikes down the usurper Ragha Moran with a sword blow from behind; loyalist nobles storm the palace and liberate King Lakshmi Singha.

scenes.title: Annexation of the Chutia Kingdom
scenes.summary: Chutia forces routed at Chandangiri; Sadiya annexed into the Ahom Empire; office of Sadiya-Khowa Gohain instituted; firearms and copper-plate treasures acquired.
scenes.notes: Habung was taken in 1512 and Dhirnarayan routed at Dibru in 1523; by 1524 Phrasengmung Borgohain governed Sadiya.

scenes.title: Mula Gabharu Falls Fighting Turbak
scenes.summary: After her husband Phrasengmung Borgohain is killed by Turbak's army, Princess Mula Gabharu leads women warriors into battle and is killed with five companions. Her death rallies the Ahom army.
scenes.notes: Wikipedia names the Battle of Kachua; much of the story (the Kin Lao vow, her speech) is legend.

scenes.title: Birth of Konseng in the Naga Foothills
scenes.summary: The exiled queen gives birth to prince Konseng among the Nagas, raised in mountain traditions before returning to court.

scenes.title: Konseng's Return and Presentation to King Suhungmung
scenes.summary: Grown into a stalwart warrior, Konseng is brought from the Naga village to Bakata; Suhungmung acknowledges him as half-brother of royal blood.

scenes.title: Creation of the Office of Barpatragohain
scenes.summary: Suhungmung creates a third great ministerial post—the Barpatragohain—elevating Konseng to equal rank with Burhagohain and Borgohain.

scenes.title: Konseng Fortifies the Western Border
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain deploys stockades, signal towers, and cannon batteries along the western border to counter Bengal Sultanate raids.

scenes.title: Repulse of Early Bengal Sultanate Invasions
scenes.summary: Ahom armies defeat Bengal Sultanate commanders Bit Malik and Mit Manik in naval battles, capturing artillery and cavalry horses.

scenes.title: The Great Invasion of Commander Turbak
scenes.summary: General Turbak invades Assam with a large Gaur army armed with muskets, heavy cannons, and cavalry.

scenes.title: Decisive Victory Over Turbak and Pursuit to Karatoya
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain slays Turbak on the battlefield; Bengal forces routed; Ahoms pursue retreating invaders to the sacred Karatoya River.

characters.name: Ton Kham Borgohain

characters.name: Aikhek Burhagohain
characters.summary: Offered little resistance to Chilarai's 1563 invasion and was removed as Burhagohain after the Treaty of Majuli.

characters.name: Momai Tamuli Borbarua
characters.summary: Rose from humble origins to become the first Borbarua. Systematised the paik system in 1609, commanded at Duimunsila (1638) and signed the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639). Father of Lachit Borphukan.
characters.notes: The infobox gives 1664 and a category gives 1650 for his death. Character sheet is a modern scene-based reconstruction using local Paik Reforms, creation of offices and western frontier images for face and Ahom clothing.

scenes.title: Reorganization of the Paik System by Momai Tamuli Barbarua
scenes.summary: Momai Tamuli reorganizes adult males into Paik squads (Gots of 3 or 4 men), mandatory rotation of state labor, and khel guilds, transforming Assam's agrarian and military mobilization.

scenes.title: Institution of the Offices of Borbarua and Borphukan
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha creates two supreme executive posts: the Borbarua (prime administrator & chief judicial magistrate) and Borphukan (viceroy & supreme military warden of Lower Assam).

scenes.title: The Mughal War of 1636–1638
scenes.summary: Pratap Singha and Balinarayan push west to Sualkuchi and Hajo. The Mughals under Allah Yar Khan strike back and retake Kamrup; Balinarayan dies, and the Samdhara garrison and the naval fight at Duimunisila stop the Mughal advance.

scenes.title: Treaty of Asurar Ali and Western Defense Line
scenes.summary: Following repeated repulses of Mughal invasions, Pratap Singha signs the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639) with Allah Yar Khan, formalizing the Barnadi River as the frontier.

characters.name: Atan Burhagohain
characters.summary: Appointed Burhagohain in January 1662 while Mir Jumla held Garhgaon. Negotiated the Treaty of Ghilajharighat, commanded the northern division at Saraighat and twice declined the crown. Murdered in 1679 by men of Laluk Sola Borphukan.
characters.notes: Served under eight kings.

scenes.title: Chakradhwaj Singha's Oath of Resistance
scenes.summary: Receiving a patronizing Mughal royal robe (khilat) from Delhi, King Chakradhwaj angrily throws it down, proclaiming: 'Death is preferable to a state of subordination to the Bengas!'

scenes.title: Installation of Sujinphaa by Atan Burhagohain
scenes.summary: Noble statesman Atan Burhagohain refuses the crown himself and adheres strictly to constitution by placing Dihingia prince Sujinphaa on the throne.

scenes.title: Court Suspicion and Rift Between King and Premier
scenes.summary: Influenced by plotting sons and courtiers, Sujinphaa begins to view the immensely popular Atan Burhagohain with bitter suspicion.

scenes.title: The Royal Army Deserts Sujinphaa
scenes.summary: When Sujinphaa attempts an armed ambush against the Burhagohain, royal soldiers refuse to strike their beloved prime minister and desert the king.

scenes.title: Accession and Court of Sudoiphaa Paratiya Raja
scenes.summary: Paratiya prince ascends the throne; kingdom faces external intrigue from Lower Assam viceroy Laluk Sola Borphukan.

characters.name: Lachit Borphukan
characters.summary: Retook Guwahati in 1667 and led the Ahom victory over a larger Mughal fleet at Saraighat in 1671. Died the next year, and his remains lie in a maidam at Jorhat.
characters.notes: Born 24 November 1622; died 25 April 1672 at Kaliabor. Fought at Alaboi in 1669. Character sheet uses existing local Lachit scenes as visual references for face, Ahom clothing and accessories.

scenes.title: Treason of Laluk Sola: Surrender of Guwahati to the Mughals

scenes.title: Installation of the Teenaged Boy-King Sulikphaa

scenes.title: Murder of Laluk Sola Borphukan
scenes.summary: The Borphukan who sold Guwahati to the Mughals is killed by his own bodyguard, ending his hold over the boy-king Sulikphaa.

scenes.summary: Angered by the king's devotion to the ascetic Paramananda Sanyasi and his jailing of Vaishnava mahantas, Debera Hazarika and the king's brother Sarugohain storm the palace at midnight. Udayaditya is taken to Charaideo and killed; his brother takes the throne as Ramdhwaj Singha.

scenes.title: Debera Borbarua Installs and Murders the Samaguria Raja
scenes.summary: Debera poisons Ramdhwaj and installs Suhung as puppet monarch; when Suhung questions his authority, Debera assassinates him in 20 days.

scenes.title: Gobar Raja Crowned as Debera's Puppet
scenes.summary: Debera crowns Tungkhungia prince Gobar (father of Gadadhar Singha) as king to maintain his puppet grip over the throne.

scenes.title: Atan Burhagohain Captures Garhgaon and Executes Debera and Gobar
scenes.summary: Atan Burhagohain leads an army of loyalist commanders from Guwahati to Garhgaon, arrests and executes Debera and deposes Gobar.

characters.name: Krishnaram Bhattacharya Nyayavagish
characters.summary: A scholar from Nabadwip invited as religious guide under Rudra Singha; later adviser (Parbatiya Gosain) under Siva Singha.

scenes.title: Krishnaram Bhattacharya Becomes the Parbatiya Gosain
scenes.summary: Siva Singha becomes the disciple of the Nabadwip Shakta priest Krishnaram Bhattacharya and gives him charge of the Kamakhya temple on Nilachal hill, where he is known as the Parbatiya Gosain.

characters.name: Ghanashyam Khanikar
characters.summary: Named in the project catalogue as the architect behind Rudra Singha's building of Rangpur.
characters.notes: Not found in the Rudra Singha article; treat as unverified.

scenes.title: Founding and Construction of Capital City Rangpur and Joysagar
scenes.summary: Constructs the glorious capital Rangpur ('City of Joy'), excavates the massive Joysagar tank in memory of mother Joymoti, and builds Namdang stone bridge.

characters.name: Kirti Chandra Borbarua (Gendhela)
characters.summary: Held real power under Rajeswar Singha and made Lakshmi Singha king in 1769. Had the Buranjis collected and many destroyed over references to his low origins.

scenes.title: Kirti Chandra Borbarua Crowns Rajeswar Singha
scenes.summary: On Pramatta Singha's death, the Borbarua Kirti Chandra passes over the elder princes and places Rajeswar Singha on the throne, beginning two decades of his dominance at court.

scenes.title: The Burning of the Buranjis
scenes.summary: Stung by the Chakari-pheti Buranji's mockery of his low birth, Kirti Chandra Borbarua has the Buranjis collected and burns those he judges false. Some copies survive.
scenes.notes: Most sources place this under Rajeswar Singha; some under Lakshmi Singha. Numali Borgohain (author of the Chakari-pheti) is not yet in the database.

characters.name: Haranath Bitarual Phukan
characters.summary: Led the 1765 army sent to help Manipur against the Burmese; the jungle route defeated it and it became known as the War of the Creepers.

scenes.title: Lata-Katai Ran: The Mountain Expedition to Manipur
scenes.summary: Rajeswar Singha dispatches an army across trackless, creepers-choked mountain jungles ('Lata-Katai Ran') to liberate Manipur from Burmese occupation and reinstate Meitei King Jai Singh.

characters.name: Purnananda Burhagohain
characters.summary: Placed Kamaleswar and then Chandrakanta on the throne and ran the state for two decades. Collapsed and died on 27 March 1817 on learning that Badan Chandra Borphukan was with the Burmese.
characters.notes: His eldest son Ruchinath succeeded him as Burhagohain.

scenes.title: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

scenes.title: Second Moamoria Rebellion: Fall and Burning of Rangpur
scenes.summary: Rebels rise again with devastating ferocity, routing royal armies, storming and burning royal buildings of Rangpur.

scenes.title: The Capital Moves from Rangpur to Jorhat
scenes.summary: With Rangpur wrecked by the rebellion, the Ahom court moves its capital to Jorhat, which stays the last capital of the kingdom.
scenes.notes: Sources disagree on whether the move was completed before or after Gaurinath's death.

scenes.title: The Autocratic Regency of Premier Purnananda Burhagohain
scenes.summary: Purnananda Burhagohain exercises de facto sovereign rule, establishing Jorhat as new capital, drilling troops with modern British flintlocks, and suppressing insurrections.

scenes.title: Matak Autonomy: Sarbananda Made Barsenapati
scenes.summary: After a stalemate at Bengmara, Purnananda Burhagohain recognises Sarbananda as Barsenapati of an autonomous Matak rajya paying annual tribute. The Moamoria rebellion ends.

scenes.title: Deadly Court Factionalism Between Burhagohain and Borphukan
scenes.summary: Young Chandrakanta Singha sides with favorite Satram against the elderly Purnananda; Badan Chandra Borphukan conspires against the premier.

scenes.title: Badan Chandra Borphukan Goes to the Court of Ava
scenes.summary: Hunted by Purnananda Burhagohain, Badan Chandra flees to Bengal, is refused help by the East India Company, and reaches the Burmese king Bodawpaya to ask for an army.

scenes.title: The First Burmese Invasion (Manor Din Begins)
scenes.summary: Badan Chandra brings a Burmese army of 16,000 soldiers across the Patkai; Purnananda dies of heartbreak; Burmese defeat Ahom troops at Ghiladhari and march on Jorhat.

scenes.title: Assassination of Traitor Badan Chandra Borphukan
scenes.summary: Subedar Rup Singh strikes down Badan Chandra Borphukan with a dao while bathing in Jorhat, executing retribution for bringing Burmese invaders.

scenes.title: Piyali Phukan and Jiuram Dulia Baruah Hanged
scenes.summary: A plot to drive the British out and restore Ahom rule is uncovered. Piyali Phukan, son of Badan Chandra Borphukan, and Jiuram Dulia Baruah are hanged.
scenes.notes: Sources differ on the day and place (August or 23 September 1830; Sivasagar or Jorhat) and on Jiuram's name (Dulia Baruah or Medhi). Piyali and Jiuram are not yet in the database; badan-chandra-borphukan is linked only as his father.

characters.name: Ruchinath Burhagohain
characters.summary: Eldest son of Purnananda; became Burhagohain in 1817, deposed Chandrakanta in February 1818 and installed Purandar Singha, and later sought British help.

scenes.title: Deposition of Chandrakanta and Accession of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Ruchinath Burhagohain captures Jorhat, slits Chandrakanta's right ear to permanently disqualify him from kingship, and crowns Purandar Singha.

scenes.title: Second Burmese Invasion and Flight of Purandar Singha
scenes.summary: Burmese monarch sends large army under Ala Mingi; Purandar and Ruchinath are routed at Nazira and flee into British Bengal territory.

characters.name: Subedar Rup Singh
characters.summary: Killed Badan Chandra Borphukan, in a plot backed by the queen-mother.

characters.name: Ragha Neog (Raghab Borbarua)
characters.summary: Flogged over elephant levies in September 1769, which sparked the revolt. Became Borbarua and was killed in April 1770 by nobles aided by Kuranganayani.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Moamoria Rebellion
scenes.summary: Enraged by insults to their Guru, peasant masses and Moran disciples of the Moamoria Satra revolt, routing royal forces and capturing the capital Rangpur.

scenes.title: Captivity and Imprisonment of King Lakshmi Singha
scenes.summary: Rebels capture Swargadeo Lakshmi Singha, imprison him at the Joysagar temple, and declare Ramakanta as ruler and Ragha Moran as Barbarua.

scenes.title: Queen Kuranganayani's Daring Counter-Coup
scenes.summary: During Rongali Bihu, Queen Kuranganayani bravely strikes down the usurper Ragha Moran with a sword blow from behind; loyalist nobles storm the palace and liberate King Lakshmi Singha.

characters.name: Naharkhora Saikia
characters.summary: Co-leader with Ragha; helped install his son Ramakanta as rebel king and was executed in the 1770 purge.

scenes.title: Outbreak of the First Moamoria Rebellion

characters.name: Ramakanta
characters.summary: Naharkhora's son, placed on the throne by the rebels in November 1769 and executed in 1770.

scenes.title: Captivity and Imprisonment of King Lakshmi Singha
scenes.summary: Rebels capture Swargadeo Lakshmi Singha, imprison him at the Joysagar temple, and declare Ramakanta as ruler and Ragha Moran as Barbarua.

characters.name: Harihar Tanti
characters.summary: Reorganised the Dafla-Bhatia rebels in 1786 and administered the north bank of the Brahmaputra.

scenes.title: Harihar Tanti's Rising and the Burning of the Majuli Satras
scenes.summary: The rebellion resumes from the Dafla hills under Harihar Tanti, joined by Pitambar. Rebels burn the satras of Majuli and march on Rangpur.

characters.name: Bharat Singha
characters.summary: Moamoria chief placed on the throne after the 1785–86 rebel victory; coins were struck in his name. Killed in 1799 (another page gives 1800).

scenes.title: Bharat Singha Crowned at Rangpur
scenes.summary: With Gaurinath in exile at Guwahati, the Moamorias install Bharat Singha as king at Rangpur. He strikes coins claiming descent from Bhagadatta, and is killed in 1799.
scenes.notes: Coins in his name are dated 1789–94 and 1796–97.

characters.name: Sarbananda Singha
characters.role: Rebel ruler of the Moran tracts
characters.summary: Ruled the Moran tracts from Bengmara. After fighting royalists in 1805 he accepted peace, became Barsenapati and governed the autonomous Matak kingdom.

scenes.title: Sarbananda Singha's Capital at Bengmara
scenes.summary: The Moamoria leader Sarbananda Singha takes the title Swargadeo and moves his capital from Rangagarah to Bengmara in present-day Tinsukia.

scenes.title: Matak Autonomy: Sarbananda Made Barsenapati
scenes.summary: After a stalemate at Bengmara, Purnananda Burhagohain recognises Sarbananda as Barsenapati of an autonomous Matak rajya paying annual tribute. The Moamoria rebellion ends.

scenes.title: Repulse of Early Bengal Sultanate Invasions
scenes.summary: Ahom armies defeat Bengal Sultanate commanders Bit Malik and Mit Manik in naval battles, capturing artillery and cavalry horses.

scenes.title: The Great Invasion of Commander Turbak
scenes.summary: General Turbak invades Assam with a large Gaur army armed with muskets, heavy cannons, and cavalry.

scenes.title: Decisive Victory Over Turbak and Pursuit to Karatoya
scenes.summary: Konseng Barpatragohain slays Turbak on the battlefield; Bengal forces routed; Ahoms pursue retreating invaders to the sacred Karatoya River.

scenes.title: Mula Gabharu Falls Fighting Turbak
scenes.summary: After her husband Phrasengmung Borgohain is killed by Turbak's army, Princess Mula Gabharu leads women warriors into battle and is killed with five companions. Her death rallies the Ahom army.
scenes.notes: Wikipedia names the Battle of Kachua; much of the story (the Kin Lao vow, her speech) is legend.

scenes.title: Night Attack at Samdhara: Abu Bakr's Fleet Destroyed
scenes.summary: The first Mughal invasion under Sayyid Abu Bakr and Satrajit takes Kajali, then is destroyed in a night attack by the Bharali–Brahmaputra confluence. Abu Bakr is killed, Satrajit escapes, and Pratap Singha builds a fort at Samdhara inscribed 'Victory in Unequal Battle'.

scenes.title: The Mughal War of 1636–1638

scenes.title: Treaty of Asurar Ali and Western Defense Line
scenes.summary: Following repeated repulses of Mughal invasions, Pratap Singha signs the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639) with Allah Yar Khan, formalizing the Barnadi River as the frontier.

scenes.title: Mir Jumla's Imperial Mughal Invasion
scenes.summary: Aurangzeb's premier general and Viceroy of Bengal, Mir Jumla, advances up the Brahmaputra with 12,000 cavalry, 30,000 infantry, and 323 armed war boats.

scenes.title: Mughal Capture of Capital Garhgaon
scenes.summary: Mir Jumla enters Garhgaon in victory; thousands of Ahom cannons, gold treasures, and grain reserves are captured by imperial Mughal forces.

scenes.title: The Monsoon Counter-War of Namrup

scenes.title: The Treaty of Ghilajharighat
scenes.summary: Severely ill Mir Jumla and exhausted Jayadhwaj sign treaty; Ahoms cede Western Assam, pay war indemnities of gold, silver, 90 elephants, and send princesses.

scenes.title: Death of Mir Jumla on the Return March
